signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish BoJ Repricing
signals.text: NZD/JPY trades under acute downside pressure as JPY dominates the G10 space following explicit hawkish guidance from BoJ's Masu. Masu stated the central bank must raise rates further to estimated neutral levels promptly, driving massive repricing across JPY crosses ahead of the 18 Sep BoJ decision. The 1W G10 scorecard flags a critical bilateral divergence: JPY leads G10 (+1.487% avg, n=7) while NZD lags as the bottom G10 performer (-0.906% avg, n=4), yielding a 2.393% spread. NZD/JPY spot sits cheap at fair value z=-3.11σ, while CFTC data shows JPY leveraged short positioning stretched at pctl 2 (lev net -111,297), leaving massive short-squeeze fuel for JPY as monetary normalization accelerates. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, driven by hawkish BoJ repricing against a weak NZD backdrop. Catalyst: BoJ Rate Decision on 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ holds policy rate unchanged without hawkish guidance, sparking a sharp unwind of recent JPY gains.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Hawkish BoJ Repricing + Volatility Compression
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.390, remaining below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (158.16/159.98/158.42) as hawkish rhetoric from BoJ Board Member Masu drives JPY buying across the board. The 266bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98%) continues to favor USD, but a -2.31 25d Risk Reversal highlights significant institutional demand for USD/JPY downside protection. Options market pricing displays unusual complacency with IV at 10.8% trading below HV30 at 11.3% (VRP -0.6%), suggesting potential for a volatility expansion if downside momentum accelerates. Positioning remains extreme with JPY COT net short at -111,297 (pctl 2, z -2.18) while retail stands 86% long USD/JPY, setting up a severe contrarian unwinding setup. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, driven by hawkish BoJ rhetoric overriding carry support. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US CPI significantly exceeds expectations, reigniting USD yield support.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Carry Support
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.72250, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7159/0.7060/0.6998) backed by strong fundamental and carry tailwinds. The 71bp OIS carry premium (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%) favors AUD, supported by a positive ESI reading of +17.3 reflecting steady domestic data beats. However, CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds crowded long at +50,250 net contracts (pctl 94, z +1.79) with WoW flow stalling (-3,328 contracts), while retail sentiment sits at an extreme 91% short, creating institutional-versus-retail divergence near multi-month highs. Options pricing shows 1M IV at 7.1% against HV30 of 5.9% (VRP +1.2%), pointing to moderate demand for downside hedging against upside trend exhaustion. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD, carry-supported trend with late-stage positioning caution. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp risk-off sentiment spike forcing liquidation of crowded speculative longs.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CB Policy Divergence + Low Volatility
signals.text: EUR/USD trades quietly at 1.16430, hovering above its SMA20 (1.1625) and SMA50 (1.1525) but below its SMA200 (1.1637). Carry continues to favor USD via a +145bp OIS spread (SOFR 3.64% vs €STR 2.19%), though market pricing anticipates a potential ECB hike at today's decision while the Fed remains on hold at 3.75%. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net short EUR position of -52,784 contracts (pctl 31), showing balanced structural positioning, while options vol remains subdued with 1M IV at 5.0% vs HV30 at 4.2% (VRP +0.8%) and a neutral 25d RR (-0.11). Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD, awaiting central bank catalysts to establish directional momentum. Catalyst: ECB Policy Decision and Press Conference today at 12:15/12:45 UTC. Risk: ECB delivers a dovish hold, triggering a sharp re-pricing lower toward SMA50 support.
